## Reasoning
Bob's spouse Alice died in 2014, so Bob is unmarried for 2018 (§7703(a)(1)). Bob qualifies as Head of Household because he maintains a household for Charlie, who is a qualifying relative (Charlie had no income, was not anyone's dependent, lived with Bob all year, and Bob provided support). Bob's AGI is $304,598, exceeding the HOH phaseout threshold of $275,000 (§68(b)(B)). The excess of $29,598 creates 12 increments ($29,598/$2,500 = 11.84, rounded up), resulting in a 24% applicable percentage (§151(d)(3)). Each $2,000 exemption is reduced to $1,520, for total exemptions of $3,040. Standard deduction for HOH is $18,000 (§151(d)(7)). Taxable income = $304,598 - $18,000 - $3,040 = $283,558. Tax under §1(b)(v): $77,485 + 39.6% × ($283,558 - $250,000) = $77,485 + $13,288.97 = $90,773.97, rounded to $90,774.
